To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the light yield of liquid xenon can be improved to 10 photoelectrons/keV by purification, and that the energy resolution of 3.5% at 662 keV can be achieved for a 1 kg detector with a light yield of 10 photoelectons/keV.
the absorption length of scintillation photons in liquid xenon is longer than 100 cm, and this length is sufficient for a 800 l detector for the MEG II experiment.

the scintillation absorption in liquid xenon can be suppressed to a negligible level by suitable purification and that the expected energy resolution for the 100 l liquid xenol γ -ray detector for the MEG is 0.6 %.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an 800 l xenon detector for the MEG detector, and we have studied the light absorption in xenon.
the development of a large-scale liquid xenon scitation detector and with the purification technique of xenon.
a study of the absorption of scintillation photons by impurities in liquid xenon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the light absorption is negligible for the MEG detector.
the absorption length of the scintillation photon is longer than 100  cm in our detector, and that this absorption length is not a critical parameter in our experiment.
the absorption of light is not a limiting factor for the performance of the detector.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a 100  l liquid xenon detector can achieve an energy resolution of 1.5% ( F W H M / E 0 ) at 1 MeV, which is comparable to that of a 10 l liquid xenon prototype detector.
the energy resolution is not limited by the absorption of scintillation lights in the present 800 l detector design.
a liquid xenon γ -ray detector of the size of 800 l is feasible with a good energy resolution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy resolution is expected to be better than 2% for 1 MeV γ -rays, even if the absorption length is as low as 10 cm.
a large volume liquid xenon detector can be built without the need for an optical reflector, which is a major source of background for the experiment.
the light absorption in a liquid xenon γ -ray detector will not be a serious problem, even for a 1000 l detector, if the liquid xenon is sufficiently purified.
